title: Churn: ten drop-and-reconnect and graceful-leave-and-rejoin cycles leave no ghost entity, no extra player and no Redis key
description: map_01, enemies standing still and harmless. Two rendered clients stay in the world and observe: one walks 4 s out and 4 s back (it stays inside the 50-unit area of interest of the churn users), one stands still. From 8 s a raw-client harness step (lab/rawprobe.py) runs 10 cycles through the real join path (gateway auth, enter world, KCP join): odd cycles use user A and DROP (both sockets closed with no MsgDisconnect, the way a killed process ends) and rejoin 3 s later; even cycles use user B and LEAVE gracefully (MsgDisconnect) and rejoin 6 s later. Each cycle stays connected for 4 s. After the last cycle the step waits 80 s, longer than the server needs to notice a silent peer (PingInterval 10 s + PongTimeout 30 s) plus the 30 s map hold (EntityHoldTTL), then reads Redis again. Redis session, registry and map-member key names are read once before the first cycle and once after the wait. Graded: every cycle joined; no player entity nobody owns; a graceful leaver is gone for the server and for both rendered clients within 5 s; the dropped user is gone by 75 s after its last drop; in the quiet window the server holds exactly the rendered clients' entities and each rendered client draws exactly the rendered clients' players; players_online and connections return to the baseline; no Redis key leaked.

assertions.title: no ghost entity: the leaver and the dropped player disappear for everyone, nobody else appears
players_online and connections return to the baseline
no leaked Redis session, registry entry or map member
no removed entity is still drawn, no id drawn twice
the rendered clients see no session close
